# workbuddy2everything
**English** | 简体中文
> **The repository is now `workbuddy2everything`. The npm package name stays `dsh-workbuddy-codex`.*
* GitHub redirects the old URL, so existing clones and `github:` dependencies keep working — nothing
needs reinstalling.
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a local WorkBuddy gateway into **a model backend for every clie
nt** — the model picker's provider, the gateway behind it, **and the two protocol bridges: Responses
for OpenAI Codex CLI, Anthropic Messages for Claude Code and Claude Desktop**.
These have to line up before a WorkBuddy model can answer, and none of them installs itself as a Win

laude Code and Claude Desktop 3p |

om `dsh-llm-workbuddy`** |
These processes used to be started by hand, so a reboot silently left the model picker pointing at a
dead port — the provider plugin loaded fine, listed models fine, and failed on the first request. T
his plugin supervises them: on load it probes each health endpoint, spawns whatever is missing, and
re-checks on a timer so a crashed process comes back.

## Why the bridge is bundled
`codex-cli` 0.1xx+ dropped `wire_api = "chat"` and speaks **only** the OpenAI Responses API (`POST /
v1/responses`, SSE). A WorkBuddy gateway implements **only** Chat Completions (`POST /v1/chat/comple
tions`). Point Codex straight at the gateway and every request dies with:

There is no config flag around this — Codex rejects `wire_api = "chat"` at load time. A translation
layer is mandatory, so this package ships one:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It is the same code as codex-chat-bridge, vendored at `bridge/codex-chat-bridge.mjs` (zero dependenc
ies, runs on the harness's own Node) so installing this plugin is the only step — there is no second

### Why the model ids are rewritten as `claude-wb-…`
Desktop runs every discovered row through a filter (`No()`): an id carrying another vendor's brand t
oken (`kimi`, `gpt`, `deepseek`, `qwen`, `glm`, …) is dropped outright, and the id must also look li
ke an Anthropic route (`claude…`). A real `cn:kimi-k3.1-pro` fails both — the picker comes up empty.
So the bridge hashes the real id into `claude-wb-<10 hex>` and publishes that, keeping the real id o
nly in its in-memory catalog, while **the human-readable name rides in `display_name`** (`CN · Kimi-
K3.1-Pro`). When a `claude-wb-…` comes back, the bridge maps it to the real id and forwards that.
One more trap: Desktop merges picker rows by `(name, Anthropic family)`. Several distinct gateway mo
dels share one display name (`cn:hy3` / `cn:hy3-x`, `cn:hy4-preview` / `cn:hy4-preview-f`, …), so co
pying the names verbatim **silently hides rows**. The bridge therefore appends the distinguishing ta
il of the id, but only where names actually collide: `CN · Hy3 (x)`, `Global · Auto (chat)`. Measure
d against this gateway: 52 models in, 52 rows in the picker.
## Why a local prompt ceiling
An upstream `400 prompt_too_long` is not just a rejection — it returns **no `usage`**. A client that
learns its own size from `usage` therefore cannot see how far over it is. It holds the last success
ful measurement, keeps resending the same oversized history, and never reaches the threshold that wo
uld trigger auto-compaction. Measured on a real session: the last success was `662,937` input tokens
, the rejected body was `1,049,429`, and the client's counter stayed frozen at `662,937` — 70% of a
950k window — for the rest of the session. The overshoot was 849 tokens, and it was unrecoverable.
Two consequences the bridge handles directly:
- **Images in tool results are re-attached, not serialized.** A Chat Completions `role: "tool"` mess
age carries text only, so an image returned by a tool has nowhere to go. Stringifying it put the who
le `data:` URL into the prompt as literal text; the upstream tokenizer then charged roughly one toke
n per character. One 1080p screenshot (~570k base64 characters) was measured at 280k–594k input toke
ns — a single tool result could fill a 1M context. The bridge now keeps the text in the tool message
, notes that images moved, and re-attaches them as real `image_url` parts on the next user message (
after the whole run of tool results, so the assistant `tool_calls` pairing is not broken). Measured
after the fix: the same 762,772-character screenshot costs **1,100** input tokens instead of 594,443
, and the model reads the image normally. At most 8 images are hoisted per tool result; the rest are

reported by count.
- **`maxPromptTokens` refuses locally.** Above the ceiling the bridge answers `4
13` with the estimated size and never contacts the upstream. No account is spent, no rate-limit cool
down is tripped, and the message says what to do.
Set it a little **above** the real ceiling (`1200000` for a `1048576`-token upstream) so an estimate
that runs high cannot refuse a request that would have fit. The estimate is deliberately crude — ~4
chars/token for text, ~1 char/token for long base64 runs, a fixed vision cost per image — which is
why it is a tripwire and not a context manager.
